video_title: Carmelo Anthony on Wemby's Takeover, Knicks Finals Chances & Kiyan's Tough Freshman Year

quotes.speaker: Carmelo Anthony
quotes.summary_phrase: Carmelo Anthony's media transition and desire for authentic sports talk
quotes.excerpt: My experience is totally different than anybody else's experience. I don't have the same experience as other people.
quotes.quote: Man, like honestly, it's been amazing to just go through that journey, right? We all retired, you guys know that, that transition period of what it takes to really figure out what's next. I got a chance to do it earlier than most people. I got a chance to start locking in mentally like what I want to do, putting a plan together. Again, this whole media Melo thing, like I've never saw myself doing this. The people were calling, I'm like, man, I'm not doing that. Listen, y'all want me to go out there and talk? I'm not talking. Y'all don't want to hear what I got to say. But then as I started being around the kids and just the youth in EBYL and the circuits and being in Bmore and my teams, you get a different connection. I got a different connection to the game and I got a chance to see the game at a whole different from a whole different landscape, from a younger generation. So now I get to see it from grassroots and development all the way up to the professional leagues, all the way up to international. So I'm in the game, so I'm like, it's only right for me to just go in and talk the game, but do it my way. I don't want to do it the way that nobody else do it. I want to support people that's going, that's out there, you know, talking the game. But my experience is totally different than anybody else's experience. I don't have the same experience as other people. We all played ball, but I don't have the same experience. So I want to talk about things that I've been through, things that I've seen, things that I've participated in, and that's it. And I'll give you my honest opinion and it's going to always be genuine, it's going to always be real because I want to help everybody that's in whatever situation that they're in. But also, if you're messing up, pardon the French, if you're messing up, then you're messing up. We can't do nothing about that. We still got to hold you accountable.

quotes.speaker: Carmelo Anthony
quotes.summary_phrase: Carmelo Anthony expresses awe for Victor Wembanyama's unprecedented talent and mindset
quotes.excerpt: We've never seen nothing like Wemby. I don't care what it is. Man, this guy's in his first three seasons.
quotes.quote: Oh, bro, we've seen a lot of nice guys come through this league. We've seen the best of the best. We've played against the best of the best, and we pay homage to who came before us. We stand on them shoulders of giants. With that being said, we've never seen nothing like Victor Wembanyama. We've never seen nothing like Wemby. I don't care what it is. Man, this guy's in his first three seasons. We don't know what he's going to be. He was mad that Shai Gilgeous-Alexander got the MVP last night. He came out, he stood on business, he said it, I'm mad, I don't like that he got it, that's supposed to have been mine. People are going to talk about how tall he is and what he could do. No, no, no, no. We're going to talk about the mindset that he got. We've never seen no young players coming in this league saying, I want the MVP, it should be mine, I'm going to take it, Defensive Player of the Year is mine, this, this, and that, my team is going to win 60 wins. We don't hear stuff like that. We heard that from Muhammad Ali. You get what I'm saying? And we fell in love, we love Muhammad Ali for his brashness. This ain't brashness right here. This is a young kid who really understands what it means to be the face of the NBA internationally, globally. He understands that. And everything that comes with that. And I've never seen nothing like that, champ. He did, he caught a lob, he was standing on the ground, Chet was on his left arm, he just reached up and dunked. Like, I've never seen nothing like that. And then just to add on to that, the three at the end of the game, you know how pressurized that situation is in that moment, to come down and shoot a transition three. And he came out after the game and said, I wasn't even thinking, I don't know what was going on. That's a scary sign to me. For you to be doing that and getting 40 and 20 something and five blocks and six steals, and you're not thinking? Come on. So it's, to answer the question, I've never seen anything up close and personal like that. And I came in the game with LeBron James. You get what I'm saying? And I've seen LeBron James, and we thought we ain't never seen LeBron James before. This is different. This is on a whole different level than what we felt about LeBron James.

quotes.speaker: Carmelo Anthony
quotes.summary_phrase: Carmelo Anthony praises the San Antonio Spurs' culture for developing young talent and their playoff performance
quotes.excerpt: This is a very young San Antonio team led by a 20-year-old and a 22-year-old. Their core guys are 20, 21, and 22.

text_blocks.speaker: Matt Barnes
text_blocks.text: I think what's interesting too is the youngest starting five in playoff history where the average age is almost 23, about 22 years and 300 plus days. And we came to in our league, come playoff time, experience was key. But this new generation, I mean, they're trying to debunk that. Obviously, Oklahoma City had a few knocks before they got to their stuff last year and won a chip. But this is a very young San Antonio team led by a 20-year-old and a 22-year-old. And what's Vassell, 21? I mean, their core guys are 20, 21, and 22 in a league that experience always pays dividends, but they're showing us otherwise. Speak to the youth and then obviously with that San Antonio system and the foundation that was laid by Pop and the Tims and the Manus and the Tonys and etcetera, have laid to have us see this young team almost act like they've been there before when they haven't.

text_blocks.speaker: Carmelo Anthony
text_blocks.text: That's a testament to the culture. That's a testament to what was established years ago back in the 90s. You get what I mean? So that that just doesn't fade. You just wait your time to to get the next great one. You feel me? So they have their great one. Now you get a chance to build around that. And the system is is is very, people think that it's it's chaotic or it's simple. San Antonio's system is very simple. You come in here, you work hard, you play hard, you be a professional, you do your job. That's it. So when you're able to do that, which is why Dylan Harper could come in and play that way. He was eight for 20 last night as a rookie in Game 1 of the Western Conference Finals. That tells me Mitch let him go. There's a lot of confidence he gives him. So when you when you look at that and you still look at videos of Pop meeting Wemby at the airport and going to talk to him, it's one, two in the morning. This is Pop, he's going through what he's dealing with, and you're still putting your imprint on these guys. And you you're calling Devin Vassell late at night and telling him, giving him pointers, you know, showing him video. What organization in any sport you know have that continuity across the board? So when you talk about San Antonio and their culture, it starts from the top. This culture starts from the top. We as players could create the culture, but it got to be ran from the top. And Pop been doing that. He's been winning with that formula, and this is no different. This is no different than when he had Tim Duncan and those guys. This is no, you guys were there. This is no different than those years. They're just younger, right? They don't, they don't even know what they're doing. That's the scary part. Whereas you, y'all knew what y'all were doing. Tim Duncan knew what he was doing. Manu Ginobili knew what he was doing. Pop, these guys don't know what they're doing, and they're just hooping.

quotes.speaker: Carmelo Anthony
quotes.summary_phrase: Carmelo Anthony reflects on the intensity of the 2009 Western Conference Finals against Kobe Bryant and the Lakers
quotes.excerpt: That whole experience, just from tip-off to me and Kobe locking in at the beginning of the game.
quotes.quote: Listen, I walked out there last night like I was back in 08, 09 Western Conference Finals. It felt like it. I love these moments. But no, going back to that, man, it was again, as a team that year, man, we felt like we had an opportunity to make that run. We had an opportunity to get out the West that year. And we went through everything in building our team, the team up to that point. You know, I came in, I got drafted in 03. Those that that Finals Western Conference Finals like 08, 09. So you're talking about four, five years of just like trying to get there and building and building and building. Then you're going from losing in the first round for three, four seasons to going to the Western Conference Finals in that switch, right? So I had to look back and see what was the switch. Yes, Chauncey Billups was a was a major, major part of that team. But also, we had a really good group of guys. Like, you know, just a brotherhood off the court, on the court. And we had depth on our team. Like, we had a bench on our team. And we really felt like, oh, we can get the Lakers that year. We really believed that we could get the Lakers. So I know what Wemby is feeling right now when you beat a team in regular season, you go into postseason feeling like you can, we got their number. But that whole experience, bro, just from tip-off to me and Kobe locking in at the beginning of the game, and he telling me, let's go, you're here now, let's go. And I'm looking at this, man, what? Like, Western Conference Finals with the Lakers, Kobe, me? No, come on, baby. So it was just that experience, man, just going through it and and the preparation that it took to compete against, you know, not just the Lakers, but Kobe himself. And also Phil Jackson, man, like Phil Jackson as a coach, you got to, you got to prepare for him too as a player. Like, I had to prepare for Phil, I had to think about what Phil was trying to do. Kobe was trying to do. Sometimes they were on two different pages, so you didn't know what was going on in the game. But that was probably one of my like, greatest, greatest experience in the NBA.

quotes.speaker: Carmelo Anthony
quotes.summary_phrase: Carmelo Anthony believes the New York Knicks have the right formula to reach the NBA Finals
quotes.excerpt: I do believe that the Knicks get to the Finals this year. I've said this at the beginning of the season.
quotes.quote: Man, the Knicks gradually got better in the playoffs. It seemed like they started to get healthy. They they started to figure out different styles of play and and get prepared themselves for what's about to come. I think the Atlanta series against the Knicks prepared them to go up against Cleveland. And I say that because Atlanta had a guard like CJ McCollum who was, he was head hunting up there. He was ready to whatever mismatch he was looking for, he wanted, he was going to get. And they proved that it could work. That formula could work. Now, Atlanta ran out of gas. They only had one of those guys. You're going up against Cleveland with Donovan Mitchell. He's one of those guys. James Harden is one of those guys. You got two guys that can can head hunt pick and rolls and matchups and and do what they do and manipulate that. So that part of the game kind of got me like, oh, what is our strategy against that? The bigs matchup, Mobley, and Jarrett Allen, Mitchell Robinson, like, who's going to win the battle of the bigs? It's going to be a grimy, grind out series for the bigs, or is Julius Randle, you coming in as the Julius Randle that swept Philly, right? Where you in the Joker position and you pass it and you're making everybody look good, or are you coming in ready to put Cleveland away? Right? Which Julius Randle are you, is coming? So, I do believe that the Knicks get to the Finals this year. I've said this at the beginning of the season. I I said Knicks, Denver in the Finals. This was a while ago. But I do believe the Knicks have the the right formula to be playing in June in in in the Finals. They got defense, they got three-point shooting, they got a closer, a killer in Jalen Brunson. And Julius Randle, no matter what people think about Julius Randle, Julius Randle go out there and you look up, I got 25, 12. You're like, how the heck Julius Randle got 25 and 12? But Julius Randle got 25 and 12. So, OG Anunoby, we need OG Anunoby back and Mikal Bridges. What Mikal Bridges is going to show up? Is Mikal Bridges from Atlanta going to show up, or Mikal Bridges from Philadelphia going to show up? Those are my takes on on the series. Knicks in seven.

quotes.speaker: Stephen Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen Jackson and Matt Barnes predict a better Game 2 for the Thunder after a poor Game 1
quotes.excerpt: I think Game 2 they're going to play a lot better. They're going to be way more solid, make better plays, take care of the ball.

text_blocks.speaker: Matt Barnes
text_blocks.text: So the spread is six, six and a half for San Antonio. So you're taking the points or you're just taking San Antonio period?

text_blocks.speaker: Stephen Jackson
text_blocks.text: I'm taking San Antonio period, but for the for this segment, I'm taking the points.

text_blocks.speaker: Matt Barnes
text_blocks.text: Six and a half. We'll see if Oklahoma City can rebound. I got the Spurs as well with the six and a half points.

text_blocks.speaker: Stephen Jackson
text_blocks.text: I don't think it's going to be an overtime. I don't think they're going to bounce back. I think San Antonio won that game and they didn't even play well. A lot of turnovers, a lot of bad decisions. It's a young team, first game in the Western Conference Finals on the road. They had a little jitters. I think Game 2 they're going to play a lot better. They're going to be way more solid, make better plays, take care of the ball. And I think it's going to be an easier win this time. I don't think it's going to be an overtime.

quotes.speaker: Stephen Jackson
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen Jackson describes Gregg Popovich's father-figure role in developing young San Antonio Spurs players
quotes.excerpt: I think he's having the conversations with them, one as a father figure, but also as a guy who's continuing to give them confidence.

text_blocks.speaker: Matt Barnes
text_blocks.text: So going home 2-0 as the Spurs, how would you feel going to Game 3 up 2-0?

text_blocks.speaker: Stephen Jackson
text_blocks.text: Finish the job. You got to finish the job. I mean, obviously, this is the defending champs. They got the two-time MVP on their team. They got, you know, Williams back. But that boy Wemby is different. And De'Aaron Fox should be back at some point this series. Dylan Harper is playing great. Cassius Stanley is playing well. Their supporting cast, Miss Johnson, have these boys hitting on all cylinders at the right time. So, I feel like San Antonio wins this series in no more than five, possibly six.

text_blocks.speaker: Matt Barnes
text_blocks.text: We talk about this organization. If they're able to go up 2-0, Matt, and on, I guarantee you the sense of urgency and the importance of Game 3 back home is going, they are, they're going to fully understand that. And the sense of the fans.

text_blocks.speaker: Stephen Jackson
text_blocks.text: Exactly. What have you seen from like, uh, Pop kind of seems like he's like the mafia figure now in the background. Like, you saw when Wemby came off the plane after he had the elbow, he pulled him to the side, just what are you hearing or seeing there? And then what do you think Pop's talking to Mitch about behind the scenes about?

text_blocks.speaker: Matt Barnes
text_blocks.text: I really don't think Pop is really too much, uh, talking the game plan with Mitch. I think he's trusting in Mitch and and his coaching staff to do what they need to do. I don't think he's stepping on any toes there. But the relationships with Wemby and Harper and Cassius Stanley, I think he's having the conversations with them. One as a father figure, but also as a guy who's continuing to give them confidence. They're young guys. So you want to hear, I know as a young guy, I want to hear, bro, you're doing good, you're doing well. Don't worry about it. You know what I'm saying? Like, all those things that Pop has been good at for so many years that he gave to Tim Duncan, me, Ginobili, so many guys. I think he's just giving that more of that to the guys because he's not on the sidelines.

quotes.speaker: Carmelo Anthony
quotes.summary_phrase: Carmelo Anthony laments the lack of intentional skill work and positional differentiation in today's NBA
quotes.excerpt: I don't think people put in that type of intentional work. Going to a gym, just working on four spots today.
quotes.quote: I don't think people put in that type of intentional work. When I say intentional work of going to a gym, just working on four spots today. Like, that's it. Can you go through that process and not get bored with that of shooting the same shot for an hour and a half? Right? Couldn't you? What it takes to get through that. And for me, it was a, I just wanted to master the spots. Like, if you're going to say that I'm just a scorer, then I'm going to be the best scorer. Like, I don't care about all of that. I'm going to be the best scorer, and I'm going to show you why I'm the best scorer. My retirement now, I'm going to bring, I'm going to spin the block back. My retirement allows me to go back and watch all basketball now. Old school, new school, new players, old players. And then watch players that I, I think personally, are some of the best players that I love to watch. And then go back and watch the players that they say are the greatest players that's out there. And when you get an opportunity to to to measure yourself up against the skill set of a lot of these guys, you realize it's not that many people out there at 6'8", 6'7" with the skill set. Right? So for me, I can speak on that, that skill set. There's guys that I want to work with today. There's a lot of guys that I want to work with today. They say the mid-range is gone. MVP of the league, back-to-back MVP champion is the best mid-range player in the NBA. Right? Like, when it comes down to it, where is he getting to? He's getting to that left elbow, he's getting to that left block, push off, getting to the fade, bump fade. This is what we got to be teaching. How can you step on a court and go train and shoot a three first? No, I ain't even warmed up yet. We can't do that. So it's, it's about, how do you get away from the league being copycat? Like, it's a copycat league. You know, everybody runs the same system, handoffs, hand-downs, stack, you know, plays, fake, like, I don't, no, I need somebody to get to it. Every team needs somebody to be able to get to them spots and get to it.

quotes.speaker: Carmelo Anthony
quotes.summary_phrase: Carmelo Anthony advises Paolo Banchero to master his mid-range game before attempting step-back threes
quotes.excerpt: Master the mid-range game before you go out there and shoot a step-back three.
quotes.quote: I'll give you one example. Detroit versus Orlando. Right? Even though Orlando lost. Paolo Banchero, right? Everybody wanted Paolo Banchero. You should get to the mid-range. You, get to your mid-range. You're going to be successful at getting to your mid-range game. Master the mid-range game before you go out there and shoot a step-back three. Right? So today there's no, there's no differentiator between players and talent today. Right? If you're a guard, you're a guard. If you're a wing, you're a three-and-D guy. Right? Everybody's a three-and-D guy today. So it's, there's no, there's no positions no more on the court in in the game. And for me, I just enjoyed being in the gym, working on new things, working on new moves, getting my workout in, after the workout, I might be messing around, I might learn something. I might, man, let me try this step back on this fade right here. Oh, man, this feels good. Let me work on that the next day and the next day and the next day. But I don't think people have that, uh, that creativity today.

quotes.speaker: Carmelo Anthony
quotes.summary_phrase: Carmelo Anthony names Anthony Edwards, Paolo Banchero, and Jonathan Kuminga as players he'd like to mentor
quotes.excerpt: I would love to work with Ant. I think Ant needs to add that component to his game.

text_blocks.speaker: Matt Barnes
text_blocks.text: You said something really interesting. I'm going to put you on the spot. Give me three guys you would love to work with that are currently in the league.

text_blocks.speaker: Carmelo Anthony
text_blocks.text: I would love to work with Ant. I think Ant needs to add that component to his game. Yeah. Um, I would love to work with Paolo Banchero. Uh, I think Paolo Banchero, he he has it. I don't think he understands how to use it and when to use it. Um, I'm trying to see who, like, who else kind of, uh, to me.

text_blocks.speaker: Stephen Jackson
text_blocks.text: You know who I think, let me let me throw one out there, Melo. Jonathan Kuminga.

text_blocks.speaker: Carmelo Anthony
text_blocks.text: Kuminga, right? If if for me, if I can get Kuminga to just slow down just a little bit, if he takes his time on those on those mismatches, to where's though, they got to, they got to, the gravity goes towards him. That's when to me, that's when he's going to take that that that next step. But Kuminga is a name that, because he has footwork, right? He's quick, he's strong, he got a quick first step. He can get by you, and he he's athletic to utilize that first step that he got. So that's that's a good name, Stak.

quotes.speaker: Carmelo Anthony
quotes.summary_phrase: Carmelo Anthony discusses guiding his son Kiyan through a challenging freshman year at Syracuse, emphasizing life lessons
quotes.excerpt: I got to be there for my son as a father, whether you win, whether you lose, whether you got 20, whether you got two.

text_blocks.speaker: Matt Barnes
text_blocks.text: Hey, real quick, before we get out of here, Papa Melo, Kiyan Anthony is finishing his first year at Syracuse. Your former teammate just took over as the head coach, Gerry McNamara. And I want to say something real quick in an era where kids run at any sign of adversity. Kids run when the coach changed. Your son had an up and down freshman year, how most freshmen have years. And the first thing I saw after the season was over is how many people were trying to tell your son, oh, you need to jump in the portal, you need to do this, you need to do that. And I was so glad he had someone like you behind them to make him understand, bro, this is a part of the journey. This builds character. This builds a lot of the stuff you're going to need if you want to get to where you're going. You have to go through these tough times and it's not always grass is not always greener on the other side. With that said, what was this year like for you as, you know, seeing him, first and foremost, as your alma mater, but just kind of seeing the up and downs of a typical freshman year in college?

text_blocks.speaker: Carmelo Anthony
text_blocks.text: Well, you you're a father first, forget anything else. You're a father first. So I got to be there for my son as a father, whether you win, whether you lose, whether you got 20, whether you got two, whether you, you know what I mean? I got, I still have to be there, and I still have to give you that message every single day, every single night as a father, because I still have to lead you. You're 18, 19. I still have to guide you. I still have to lead you as a man, as your dad. Now, the other hat I wear is somebody who actually did it at Syracuse, right? So I'm wearing these two hats, which a lot of times when I go back there for him, the player hat goes off. I'm in straight father mode. Like, I'm straight father mode. So to see him go through or deal with his freshman year this way, I sat back and I really wanted to see how he was going to handle it. Like, I want to see how you were, this is nothing what you, what you're dealing with. You're 18 years old. You're coming into one of the biggest colleges, universities in in in college, right? So, and there's a lot of history here. Your father did it. We did it. There's history here. The name is on the building. Like, this is stamped in in in etched in stone for life. So there's a lot of pressure that comes with that. So I want to see how he handled that. To me, it wasn't a failure year for him. It was something that any 18-year-old kid is going to go through in college. Also, they're not recruiting high school kids no more. You get what I'm saying? So you're being, no matter unless you're top two, three, four, five pick, you're being overlooked anyway as a high school senior coming out into college. They don't think you're ready. They don't think you're mentally ready. They don't think you're physically ready. They just don't think you're ready. They have the year that they want you, they're going to put that on you. We got him for two years. He's going to be here for two years. Oh, we see him here for three years. We're going to see him here for three years. And that's how they develop you. And that's, that's to me, that's the wrong way of developing kids. You have to communicate. Even if you you got a freshman who's not going to play today, the next day, or you know going up and down, you got to grab, you got to grab those kids, man. We can't keep letting these kids get away and and go transfer. And then we talk about mental health, right? We talk about what these kids are dealing with, being stressed out at 17, 18, 19 years old. Why the hell are you stressed out at 18 years old? You're in college playing basketball for, no, we're not going to do that. So my message with him was just life. Listen, this is what we got to deal with. If if it's anybody you could learn from, I did it at the highest level. I've dealt with this, everything you could deal with when it comes to basketball. I've dealt with every emotion possible that you can get and receive from the game of basketball. This ain't nothing, bro. I know you, I believe in you, and I and I know what we do. So let's go get back in the lab, and we're going to come back, and we're going to answer all the questions that everybody had. We, okay, you want him to put 10 pounds on? We're going to, we're up, we're up 11 right now. And that's been two months. You get what I'm saying? Okay, you want him to get faster? Listen, we're going to play, we're going to play with pace. We don't want to be fast. We want to play with pace. And there's a difference between playing fast and with pace. So now, I'm going to unlock the the the mental game of it, right? The psyche aspect of this. And now I want to see my son go have a good time and smile and play on the biggest stage. Right? You're in the ACC, Syracuse Orange, your dad went there, you wear number seven. I got you playing in Madison Square Garden this year against St. John's. Let's get to work. Let's get to work. I love it. I love it.

quotes.speaker: Carmelo Anthony
quotes.summary_phrase: Carmelo Anthony criticizes the current state of college sports, advocating for age limits and player unions
quotes.excerpt: They got to get a hold of college sports. College sports is just wild. It's a mess.

text_blocks.speaker: Matt Barnes
text_blocks.text: Last question before we get you out of here. These grown-up men playing college basketball. 25, 26, 27, with mortgages and child support and stuff. You just said it yourself, I got kids, you got a son in the, my son going through it right now. Jack, they're not necessarily recruiting at college kids anymore. I get both sides from a coaching standpoint. If I can grab someone who's 25, who's been through some stuff, I'm going to grab him over an 18-year-old, even if the 18-year-old has more potential or talent. Your thoughts, should there be a cap on how old you should be able to or how old you can be playing college sports?

text_blocks.speaker: Carmelo Anthony
text_blocks.text: Yeah, they got to get a hold of college sports. College sports is just wild. It's a mess. It's the wild, like I'm I'm I'm in it and I'm seeing it from a business standpoint, from a like, every aspect you can watch this from, it's it's a mess. And it it needs to be, it needs to get under control. The money is crazy. And I'm not knocking the money. I'm I'm one who fought for the players to get money. Like, every player should be paid and paid what they deserve. But it's like they have to figure this out because this is a business. This is this is a professional league. This is college basketball is a professional league. It's a paid league now. So these kids are making $3 million, $4 million, haven't played a game in college yet. Get like, and then that's for one year. So now, if I transfer, my number from my sophomore year is going to be higher than my freshman year. So if you make it two, I'm going to make three the next year, I'm going to make four the next year. So for me, the financial literacy part of it has to come into play. Right? They have to do something with that. And then you also just got to deem this as a, this is a a semi-pro league. This is what it is. You got to put contracts in. You got to, I know, let me tell you, let me give you a quick overview of two minutes, two seconds. If I ran Syracuse basketball, I'm taking this program. I'm investing money into the basketball program. I'm putting a CEO, I'm putting a CMO, I'm putting somebody to oversee everything. I'm putting a business development person because now I have to go out there and build this as a business. I'm putting salary caps, I'm putting all of that in there because that's what this is. You can't have programs that's making 10, 12, $15 million budgets. And then you got other programs in the same conference with a $2 million budget. The the play discrepancy is just too, that gap is just too wide. So, listen, man, go go get you some contracts. Get a union. Go get a players union. Right? They need a players union in college. Who's going to run the players union? So it's it's a lot of things that I I just sit back and I watch, and I don't, I try not to voice my opinion about it because I just want to be a fan of the game, but just when the politics come in it, it it just messes everything up.

quotes.speaker: Carmelo Anthony
quotes.summary_phrase: Carmelo Anthony argues college basketball should be treated as a semi-pro league with proper business structures
quotes.excerpt: This is a business. This is a professional league. This is college basketball is a professional league.

text_blocks.speaker: Stephen Jackson
